subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 64-year-old woman with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis has hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL and MCV 88 fL. Iron studies show serum iron 35 micrograms per deciliter, TIBC 180 micrograms per deciliter, ferritin 420 ng/mL, and transferrin saturation 19%. She has no evidence of gastrointestinal bleeding.
question: Which of the following best explains these iron study results?

options.text: Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss
Hereditary hemochromatosis
Pregnancy-related changes in iron handling
Anemia of chronic disease
Sideroblastic anemia due to alcohol use

explanation_correct: Anemia of chronic disease is characterized by decreased serum iron, decreased TIBC, increased ferritin, and normal or decreased transferrin saturation. Inflammation, including increased IL-6, raises hepcidin release from the liver; hepcidin binds ferroportin on intestinal mucosal cells and macrophages and inhibits iron transport. This reduces iron release from macrophages and iron absorption from the gut, trapping iron in storage. Ferritin is an acute phase reactant and is elevated despite adequate or increased total body iron. Treating the underlying inflammatory condition is the mainstay of therapy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Iron deficiency shows increased TIBC and decreased ferritin, whereas this patient has a low TIBC and a high ferritin.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hemochromatosis shows increased serum iron, increased ferritin, and markedly increased transferrin saturation, not low iron and low saturation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Pregnancy or oral contraceptive use produces normal serum iron and ferritin, increased TIBC, and decreased saturation, not a high ferritin with low TIBC.
explanation_incorrect.E: Sideroblastic anemia shows increased serum iron, normal or decreased TIBC, and increased ferritin, not the low serum iron seen here.

educationalObjective: Anemia of chronic disease shows low serum iron, low TIBC, high ferritin, and normal or low saturation due to hepcidin-mediated iron sequestration.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 26-year-old woman with menorrhagia has a microcytic anemia. Iron studies show decreased serum iron, increased TIBC, decreased ferritin, and transferrin saturation of 8%. She reports fatigue and pica.
question: Which of the following iron study patterns is most consistent with iron deficiency anemia?

options.text: Decreased iron, decreased TIBC, increased ferritin
Increased iron, decreased TIBC, increased ferritin
Decreased iron, increased TIBC, decreased ferritin
Normal iron, increased TIBC, normal ferritin
Increased iron, increased TIBC, increased ferritin

explanation_correct: Iron deficiency produces decreased serum iron, increased TIBC, decreased ferritin, and decreased transferrin saturation, often markedly so. TIBC indirectly measures transferrin, and the liver increases transferrin synthesis when iron is deficient, raising TIBC. Ferritin, the primary iron storage protein, falls as stores are depleted. This pattern reflects chronic blood loss, malabsorption, or increased demand, and the low saturation occurs because circulating iron is low while binding capacity is high.

explanation_incorrect.A: Decreased iron, decreased TIBC, and increased ferritin describe anemia of chronic disease, not iron deficiency.
explanation_incorrect.B: Increased iron, decreased TIBC, and increased ferritin describe hemochromatosis with a primary iron disturbance and high saturation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Normal iron and ferritin with increased TIBC and decreased saturation describe the physiologic changes of pregnancy or oral contraceptive use.
explanation_incorrect.E: There is no common condition in which iron, TIBC, and ferritin are all increased; hemochromatosis has normal or decreased TIBC.

educationalObjective: Iron deficiency shows decreased serum iron, increased TIBC, decreased ferritin, and decreased transferrin saturation.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 48-year-old man has fatigue, arthralgia, and bronze pigmentation of the skin. Laboratory studies show serum iron 210 micrograms per deciliter, TIBC 240 micrograms per deciliter (normal or low), ferritin 1800 ng/mL, and transferrin saturation 88%. Liver biopsy shows increased hepatic iron deposition.
question: Which of the following best characterizes these iron studies?

options.text: A primary iron disturbance with increased iron, low or normal TIBC, increased ferritin, and markedly increased saturation
Iron deficiency with increased TIBC and decreased ferritin
Anemia of chronic disease with low TIBC and high ferritin
Pregnancy-induced changes with normal iron and ferritin
Sideroblastic anemia with low TIBC and low ferritin

explanation_correct: Hereditary hemochromatosis shows increased serum iron, decreased or normal TIBC, increased ferritin, and markedly increased transferrin saturation. The combination of increased serum iron with low or normal TIBC is the hallmark of a primary disturbance, producing the greatest rise in saturation. Unregulated intestinal iron absorption leads to deposition in liver, heart, pancreas, and joints, causing cirrhosis, cardiomyopathy, diabetes mellitus with skin pigmentation ('bronze diabetes'), arthropathy, and hypogonadism. Management includes phlebotomy and chelation when appropriate.

explanation_incorrect.B: Iron deficiency would show low serum iron, high TIBC, low ferritin, and low transferrin saturation, the opposite of this pattern.
explanation_incorrect.C: Anemia of chronic disease has low serum iron and normal or low saturation, not an iron of 210 or a saturation of 88%.
explanation_incorrect.D: Pregnancy produces normal iron and ferritin, increased TIBC, and decreased saturation, which does not fit these values.
explanation_incorrect.E: Sideroblastic anemia has increased ferritin, not low ferritin, and does not produce saturation as high as that seen in hemochromatosis.

educationalObjective: Hemochromatosis shows increased iron, low or normal TIBC, increased ferritin, and markedly increased saturation, indicating a primary iron disturbance.
source: Generated from 10. Oncology.pdf - Pathology: Interpretation of iron studies

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 28-year-old woman is in her third trimester of pregnancy. Routine laboratories show hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, serum iron within the normal range, TIBC increased, ferritin within the normal range, and transferrin saturation decreased to 16%. She takes no iron supplements and has no chronic disease.
question: Which of the following best explains this pattern of iron studies?

options.text: Iron deficiency anemia secondary to increased demand
Anemia of chronic disease
Hereditary hemochromatosis
Sideroblastic anemia
Physiologic changes of pregnancy or estrogen use with increased transferrin

explanation_correct: Pregnancy and oral contraceptive use produce a normal serum iron, increased TIBC, normal ferritin, and decreased transferrin saturation. Estrogen increases hepatic synthesis of transferrin, which raises TIBC; because serum iron stays normal, the calculated saturation falls. Ferritin remains normal because iron stores are preserved. This pattern is distinguished from iron deficiency by the normal serum iron and normal ferritin, and it is not a primary iron disturbance because saturation is decreased rather than markedly increased.

explanation_incorrect.A: Iron deficiency would show decreased serum iron and decreased ferritin in addition to increased TIBC, not normal iron and ferritin.
explanation_incorrect.B: Anemia of chronic disease shows decreased serum iron, decreased TIBC, and increased ferritin, the opposite of several of these values.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hemochromatosis shows increased serum iron, increased ferritin, and markedly increased saturation, not decreased saturation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Sideroblastic anemia shows increased serum iron and increased ferritin with normal or decreased TIBC, not normal iron with increased TIBC.

educationalObjective: Pregnancy and oral contraceptive use cause normal iron and ferritin with increased TIBC and decreased saturation, unlike iron deficiency where ferritin is low.
